key_insight: The paper shows that RL post-training for LLMs may not require updating the entire model: training just a single transformer layer can achieve performance comparable to full-parameter RL training. This suggests most RL adaptation is concentrated in a small part of the network rather than spread evenly across all layers.
problem_solved: It addresses the lack of understanding about how reinforcement learning improvements are distributed across transformer layers during LLM post-training, and whether updating all parameters is actually necessary.
method: Perform a systematic layer-wise study of RL training in transformer-based LLMs.
Compare full-parameter RL updates against training only selected layers, including the possibility of a single-layer update.
Analyze where RL gains originate to identify the most effective layer(s) for adaptation.
impact: For AI practitioners, this could reduce RL training cost, memory use, and implementation complexity while preserving performance. It also provides a practical path toward more efficient post-training and a better understanding of how LLMs adapt during RL.
visual_elements: Transformer stack diagram highlighting one trainable layer versus frozen layers
Bar chart comparing performance of full-parameter RL vs single-layer RL
Layer-wise heatmap showing where RL adaptation is strongest
Simple pipeline icon set for freeze/train/update to communicate the efficiency gain
paper_title: Is One Layer Enough? Training A Single Transformer Layer Can Match Full-Parameter RL Training
paper_authors: Zijian Zhang, Rizhen Hu, Athanasios Glentis, Dawei Li, Chung-Yiu Yau
